# SQUAB: Evaluating LLM robustness to Ambiguous and Unanswerable Questions in Semantic Parsing

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#squab)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.906.pdf) · EMNLP 2025 proceedings pp. 17926-17946

**Reading coverage:** All 21 pages, Sections 1-6 and limitations, Appendices A-E, all category examples, Tables 1-15, prompts and figure captions.

## Research question

Static public tests underrepresent schema-specific ambiguity and unsupported requests encountered on enterprise tables.

## Method

Identifies table patterns, generates relational metadata such as hypernyms or missing functions, transforms SQL templates, and verbalizes the resulting cases. Six implemented categories cover column/scope/attachment ambiguity and missing-column/calculation/out-of-scope refusal.

## Evaluation

Four LLMs on AMBROSIA-derived and 33 sampled BEAVER tables, with single-table tests and up to 10 BEAVER rows shown. Measures interpretation F1, refusal accuracy, generation cost and model-ranking agreement; one domain expert rates enterprise examples.

## What the results support

Structured synthesis yields cheaper tests and can expose failures missed by an all-LLM generator. The manual audit’s aggregate quality is high, but calculation-unanswerability correctness is rated low for 9 of 24 cases. Cost comparisons use estimated mean human annotation cost.

## Limits and qualifications

Single-table patterns do not test join reasoning. Out-of-scope functions are not programmatically proved inexpressible; failed generated SQL does not establish that no valid alternative exists. Six predefined categories require manual extension, and validation is small and single-rater.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful generator for tailored ambiguity/refusal evaluation, provided generated labels are audited rather than treated as ground-truth certificates.
